title: California Civil Code Section 2782.6 (indemnity of engineers and geologists for hazardous materials services)
publisher: California Legislative Information, Office of Legislative Counsel
claims: Section 2782.6(a) provides that nothing in subdivision (a) of Section 2782 prevents an agreement to indemnify a professional engineer or geologist, or the agents, servants, independent contractors, subsidiaries, or employees of that engineer or geologist, from liability as described in Section 2782 in providing hazardous materials identification, evaluation, preliminary assessment, design, remediation services, or other services of the types described in Sections 78125 and 78135 of the Health and Safety Code or the federal National Oil and Hazardous Substances Pollution Contingency Plan, if all of the stated criteria are satisfied.

The two criteria in subdivision (a) are that (1) the services in whole or in part address subterranean contamination or other concealed conditions caused by the hazardous materials, and (2) the promisor is responsible, or potentially responsible, for all or part of the contamination.

Subdivision (b) provides that the indemnification is valid only for damages arising from, or related to, subterranean contamination or concealed conditions, and is not applicable to the first two hundred fifty thousand dollars of liability or a greater amount as is agreed to by the parties.

Subdivision (c) provides that the section does not authorize contracts for indemnification, by promisors specified in paragraph (2) of subdivision (a), of any liability of a promisee arising from the gross negligence or willful misconduct of the promisee.

Subdivision (d) defines hazardous materials as any hazardous or toxic substance, material, or waste that is or becomes subject to regulation by any agency of the state, any municipality or political subdivision of the state, or the United States, and lists included materials such as petroleum and asbestos.

Subdivision (e) provides that nothing in the section shall be construed to alter, modify, or otherwise affect the liability of the promisor or promisee, under an indemnity agreement meeting its criteria, to third parties.
Subdivision (f) provides that the section does not apply to public entities, as defined by Section 811.2 of the Government Code.
The page carries the note 'Amended by Stats. 2022, Ch. 258, Sec. 6. (AB 2327) Effective January 1, 2023. Operative January 1, 2024, pursuant to Sec. 130 of Stats. 2022, Ch. 258.'

This section is an exception to Section 2782(a), which names it, and it concerns hazardous materials services by engineers and geologists; it is not the general design professional indemnity rule, which is Section 2782.8. Effective: 2023-01-01; operative 2024-01-01 per the page note.
